evals.prompt: The check-in system TDD is approved. The API contract is: POST /check-in accepts { user_id, user_text } and returns { basil_reply, guardrail_verdict }. Implement the backend.
evals.expected_output: Must read the project CLAUDE.md and the basil-chat-api codebase before writing anything — must understand the existing Rust/Axum handler and service patterns, the AssistantService integration, and the existing guardrail implementation. Must implement in the correct order: (1) check_ins table schema and SQLDelight/migration, (2) service layer — guardrail pre-check on user_text, Anthropic API call with companion system prompt, guardrail post-check on response, (3) Axum handler with request/response types. Must flag the companion system prompt as a required dependency — the check-in uses a different system prompt than the general assistant, and that prompt file must exist before the endpoint can be tested end-to-end. Must flag the Anthropic BAA as a blocking dependency — no user text may reach the model before the BAA is signed. Must write unit tests covering: successful submission and storage, guardrail trigger on user_text (MENTAL_HEALTH_CARD path), guardrail trigger on Basil response (EMERGENCY_CARD path), storage failure handling. Must NOT deviate from the API contract without flagging it. Must NOT hardcode the system prompt in the handler — it must be loaded from a file or config.

evals.prompt: The persistent memory TDD is approved. Implement the memory extraction and retrieval service.
evals.expected_output: Must read the basil-chat-api codebase to understand the existing ContextFn and context assembly flow before designing anything. Must implement extraction as an async background job — NOT synchronous on the live turn, to avoid adding latency. Must implement the user_memory table schema with: user_id, content (distilled fact, not verbatim quote), created_at, and row-level deletion capability (the v2 memory management UI requires this). Must implement memory retrieval with a ranking step that respects the 1,000-token budget cap — must truncate rather than overflow. Must implement graceful degradation: if the extraction job fails, the conversation continues normally and no error is surfaced to the user. Must treat all memory content as PHI — no plaintext memory entries in logs. Must flag the extraction prompt as requiring clinical review before ship (it determines what gets remembered, and extracting incorrect health patterns is a stated risk in the spec). Must write tests for: extraction result parsing, memory ranking under the token cap, graceful degradation on extraction failure, per-user scoping (no cross-user memory leakage).
